MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a multiple of 4? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 27
   C. 29
   D. 28

2. Which statement about 2,908 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is even because it ends in 8
   B. It is odd because it ends in 8
   C. It is odd because it has an even number of digits
   D. It is neither even nor odd

3. What is the 5th multiple of 6? (1 mark)
   A. 24
   B. 30
   C. 11
   D. 36

4. Which Roman numeral stands for 6? (1 mark)
   A. VIIII
   B. VI
   C. VX
   D. IIII

5. A shop sold 3,275 kg of maize in May and 4,860 kg in June. How many kilograms did it sell altogether? (1 mark)
   A. 8,125 kg
   B. 7,035 kg
   C. 8,135 kg
   D. 8,235 kg

6. What is the rule of the pattern 2,000, 2,500, 3,000, 3,500? (1 mark)
   A. add 500
   B. add 1,000
   C. add 2,000
   D. subtract 500

7. What is the sum when you add 1 to 9,999? (1 mark)
   A. 10,001
   B. 99,999
   C. 9,000
   D. 10,000

8. What is 36 × 40? (1 mark)
   A. 144
   B. 76
   C. 1,440
   D. 14,400

9. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 6 × 7 = 42? (1 mark)
   A. 7 ÷ 6 = 42
   B. 42 ÷ 6 = 6
   C. 42 ÷ 42 = 6
   D. 42 ÷ 6 = 7

10. What is 72 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 24
   B. 23
   C. 34
   D. 25

11. Write 7/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.17
   B. 0.07
   C. 0.7
   D. 7.0

12. Which decimal is the same as 3/4? (1 mark)
   A. 3.4
   B. 0.3
   C. 0.34
   D. 0.75

13. If p = 5, what is the value of 4p + 3? (1 mark)
   A. 43
   B. 23
   C. 9
   D. 12

14. If m = 7, what is the value of 6m? (1 mark)
   A. 42
   B. 67
   C. 1
   D. 13

15. A pencil starts at the 1 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 8 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 8 cm
   B. 7 cm
   C. 6 cm
   D. 9 cm

16. A rectangle is 15 cm long and 10 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 150 cm
   B. 50 cm
   C. 25 cm
   D. 52 cm

17. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 8
   C. 42
   D. 54

18. Wanjiku says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 square units. Her mistake is that she (1 mark)
   A. added instead of multiplying
   B. multiplied instead of adding
   C. forgot to use a ruler
   D. counted the corners

19. A cuboid has a volume of 48 blocks. One layer has 8 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 56
   C. 40
   D. 6

20. A beam balance is level with rice in one pan and a 1/2 kg mass and a 1/4 kg mass in the other pan. What is the mass of the rice? (1 mark)
   A. 3/4 kg
   B. 1/4 kg
   C. 1/2 kg
   D. 1 kg

21. What is 3 kg − 1 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 1 kg
   B. 1 3/4 kg
   C. 1 1/2 kg
   D. 1 1/4 kg

22. What is 1 h 20 min + 45 min? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 5 min
   B. 1 h 55 min
   C. 2 h 15 min
   D. 1 h 5 min

23. Change 210 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 3 h
   B. 4 h
   C. 4 h 30 min
   D. 3 h 30 min

24. A sweet costs 50 cents. How many sweets can you buy with Ksh 10? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 200
   C. 5
   D. 10

25. Kip faces East and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. North
   D. West

26. How many lines of symmetry does a square have? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 3
   C. 2
   D. 1

27. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. football
   B. athletics
   C. swimming
   D. netball

28. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. How many are blue or green together? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 7
   C. 5
   D. 4

29. In a tally chart, 3 groups of five and 1 more single tally mark are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 21
   B. 17
   C. 16
   D. 15

30. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 10
   C. 9
   D. 11

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write an expression for each: (a) 6 less than k, (b) three times a number b, (c) the cost of 5 pens at p shillings each. (3 marks)

32. A shopping list has 3 packets of rice at Ksh 130 each, 2 bottles of oil at Ksh 250 each and 1 tin of tomatoes at Ksh 60. Find the total cost. (4 marks)

33. Change 2 1/3 and 1 5/6 to improper fractions. (4 marks)

34. Explain the difference between area and volume. (2 marks)

35. Box P is 5 blocks long, 2 wide and 4 high. Box Q is 4 blocks long, 4 wide and 2 high. Which has the greater volume and by how many blocks? (4 marks)

36. A book cover has 12 rows of 9 squares. A notebook cover has 10 rows of 10 squares. Which cover is larger and by how many squares? (4 marks)

37. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books were left? Check your answer. (4 marks)

38. A hundred square has 60 of its small squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal. (2 marks)

39. Change 3.4 m to centimetres. (2 marks)

40. Divide 96 by 3 by dividing the tens first and then the ones. (3 marks)

41. Describe how you can use a folded piece of paper to test whether a corner is a right angle. (3 marks)

42. Write 583 in words. (2 marks)

43. A gate opens through a half turn from its closed position. Describe the angle between the gate and the wall in its closed position. (2 marks)

44. (a) Write 3 tenths and 5 hundredths as a decimal. (b) Write 7 hundredths as a decimal. (c) Arrange 0.35, 0.5, 0.07 and 0.29 from the smallest to the largest. (5 marks)

45. A sweet costs 50 cents. How many sweets can be bought with Ksh 10? (3 marks)

46. The floor of a shop has 8 rows of 12 square tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 28
   28 = 4 × 7, so 28 is a multiple of 4.

2. A — It is even because it ends in 8
   Look at the ones digit. 8 is even, so 2,908 is even.

3. B — 30
   Multiply 6 × 5 = 30. It is the 5th multiple of 6.

4. B — VI
   6 is written VI. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

5. C — 8,135 kg
   Add 3,275 + 4,860 = 8,135 kg.

6. A — add 500
   Each number is 500 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 500.

7. D — 10,000
   9,999 + 1 = 10,000. Each 9 turns into 0 and a 1 is carried to a new place.

8. C — 1,440
   36 × 4 = 144, then × 10 gives 1,440.

9. D — 42 ÷ 6 = 7
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 6 × 7 = 42, we know 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

10. A — 24
   3 × 24 = 72, so 72 ÷ 3 = 24.

11. C — 0.7
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 7/10 = 0.7.

12. D — 0.75
   3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75.

13. B — 23
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 23.

14. A — 42
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 42.

15. B — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 8 − 1 = 7 cm.

16. B — 50 cm
   Perimeter = 15 + 10 + 15 + 10 = 50 cm.

17. B — 8
   Rows × columns = 48, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

18. A — added instead of multiplying
   Area is 4 × 6 = 24 square units. She added 4 + 6.

19. D — 6
   Layers = 48 ÷ 8 = 6.

20. A — 3/4 kg
   1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 kg.

21. D — 1 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 kg − 1 3/4 kg = 1 1/4 kg.

22. A — 2 h 5 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 2 h 5 min.

23. D — 3 h 30 min
   210 ÷ 60 = 3 remainder 30, so 210 minutes = 3 h 30 min.

24. A — 20
   Ksh 10 = 1,000 cents and 1,000 ÷ 50 = 20 sweets.

25. D — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. East followed by a half turn gives West.

26. A — 4
   A square can be folded down the middle both ways and along its two diagonals.

27. A — football
   The biggest number is 5, which belongs to football.

28. A — 6
   4 + 2 = 6.

29. C — 16
   3 × 5 + 1 = 16.

30. B — 10
   Add all the numbers: 4 + 4 + 2 = 10.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) k − 6 (b) 3b (c) 5p
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct expression.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 950
   Working / marking points: 3 × 130 = 390 (1 mark); 2 × 250 = 500 (1 mark); 390 + 500 + 60 (1 mark); Ksh 950 (1 mark).

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: 7/3 and 11/6
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 × 3 + 1 = 7 so 7/3; 2 marks for 1 × 6 + 5 = 11 so 11/6.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Area is the amount of flat surface a shape covers, in square units. Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up, in cubic units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for area and 1 mark for volume.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Box P, by 8 blocks
   Working / marking points: P = 40 (1 mark); Q = 32 (1 mark); P is greater (1 mark); 40 − 32 = 8 (1 mark).

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: The book cover: 108 squares. The notebook: 100 squares. The book cover is larger by 8 squares.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for 108 and 100, 1 mark for the larger cover, 1 mark for 8.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,375 books. Check: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the subtraction with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units, 1 mark for the check.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60/100 and 0.6 (or 0.60)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the fraction and 1 mark for the decimal.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: 340 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 m = 300 cm and 0.4 m = 40 cm (1 mark). 300 + 40 = 340 cm (1 mark).

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 32
   Working / marking points: 9 tens ÷ 3 = 3 tens (1 mark); 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones (1 mark); answer 32 (1 mark).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fold a paper twice to make a neat square corner. Place its corner on the corner of the object. If it fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding to make a square corner, 1 mark for placing it on the corner, 1 mark for saying it fits exactly.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: five hundred and eighty-three
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for "five hundred and"; 1 mark for "eighty-three" spelt correctly with a hyphen.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: They make a straight line, which is two right angles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a straight line and 1 mark for two right angles.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 0.35 (b) 0.07 (c) 0.07, 0.29, 0.35, 0.5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c) (0.07 first, 0.5 last, and the middle two in order).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 sweets
   Working / marking points: Ksh 10 = 1,000 cents (1 mark); 1,000 ÷ 50 (1 mark); 20 sweets (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 96 tiles
   Working / marking points: 8 × 12 (1 mark); 80 + 16 (1 mark); 96 tiles (1 mark).
